title: Clean a scientific measurements table
intro: Create Pandas DataFrames, read typed CSV, select records, validate schemas, normalize identifiers cautiously, audit conflicting duplicates and preserve missing image-derived observations. All rows are synthetic educational data, not real biological replicates.

scientific_context.caution: These measurement tables are constructed teaching data; no direct instrument data or raw fluorescence source is implied.

chapter_method: Predict → Run → Investigate → Apply → Prove with real Pandas execution and auditable row policies.

goals.title: Create and inspect a Pandas DataFrame
goals.why: A table must keep specimen identity linked to numerical image-derived observations.
explain: A Pandas DataFrame stores named columns with potentially different dtypes. It is not merely an array of numbers.
Record IDs and measurements should remain separate: an imaging field is not necessarily a biological replicate.
DataFrame operations will remain transparent when future genuine per-image measurements are imported.

Index position is not biological replicate identity. A new filtered table should be explicitly created from the original.

Do not drop duplicate rows before assessing biological units, replicate structure and experimental provenance.

Missingness may depend on acquisition or biological condition; a convenient `.dropna()` is not automatically a scientifically justified exclusion.
